_comment: GR-2 plain-language operator texts (D-57 a). Key "ITEM:KEY" (most specific) or "*:KEY". The runner prints this text first, the exact technical instruction below it as 'details', then the picture(s). Style: one action per prompt, who does it, what to look for, safety first. Owner: Validator E.
S-00:PERSONS: Type the names of the two people at the bench: the operator (at this PC) and the observer (at the red E-stop and the 48 V switch).
S-00:COMMIT: Type the git commit printed in BUILD_INFO.txt of the gate kit.
S-00:DIP: Were the 8 DIP switches on the driver set as in the bring-up record, with the 48 V switched OFF? (y/n)
*:VERIFY-ESTOP: Look at the back of the red E-stop button. Type the terminal numbers of the two contact blocks: the NC block (wired to the board input PA10) and the NO block (wired to the 68 Ω resistor R_E). The pictures assume NC 11-12 and NO 13-14.
*:VERIFY-NUCLEO: Compare the Nucleo board with picture B7: black RESET button B2, blue USER button B1, green LED LD2, jumper JP5 on U5V. Is it the same? (y/n - if not, use the printing on the board from now on)
*:VERIFY-CELL: Look at the mechanics (nothing moves now): when the table moves AWAY from the START switch, does it PULL the spring (tension)? Picture B8. (y/n)
*:VERIFY-CALIPER: Choose two flat faces for the caliper (a fixed face at the START end and the table face toward START) and mark both with a pen. Picture B9. Done? (y/n)
*:FLASH: The product owner flashes the file named below with STM32CubeProgrammer: the .hex file, method B2, NO full-chip erase, never the .bin (picture B5). The runner has closed the COM port. When the programmer says 'verified', press Enter.
*:USB-OFF: Unplug the USB cable at the Nucleo board. The board is now off. The 48 V stays OFF.
*:USB-ON: Plug the USB cable back into the Nucleo and wait until the green LED LD2 blinks (about 2 s). Then press Enter.
HG-01:C-01: Look at the Nucleo board: is it the NUCLEO-F446RE from the old stand, with the solder bridges as listed below? Take photos of both sides. (y/n)
HG-01:PHOTO: Type the file names of the board and header photos you just took.
*:J-PUL-A: Multimeter on ohms. Measure from the J-PUL-A tap to the Nucleo pin PC7 (picture B1). Type the value (about 1000 Ω).
*:J-PUL-B: Multimeter on ohms. Measure from the J-PUL-B tap to the Nucleo pin PB7 (picture B1). Type the value (about 1000 Ω).
*:J-DIR: Multimeter on ohms. Measure from the J-DIR tap to the Nucleo pin PC9 (picture B1). Type the value (about 1000 Ω).
*:J-ENA: Multimeter on ohms. Measure from the J-ENA tap to the Nucleo pin PC8 (picture B1). Type the value (about 1000 Ω).
*:J-EVT: Multimeter on ohms. Measure from the J-EVT tap to the Nucleo pin PC6 (picture B1). Type the value (about 1000 Ω).
*:J-AUX: Multimeter on ohms. Measure from the J-AUX tap to the Nucleo pin PA11 (picture B1). Type the value (about 1000 Ω).
*:J-STIM: Multimeter on ohms. Measure from the Nucleo pin PB8 to the free plug of the J-STIM wire (pictures B1 / B3). Type the value (about 220 Ω).
HG-19:DIP: Read the 8 DIP switches on the driver from SW1 to SW8 and type them as on / off, e.g. 'on off on off off on off on'.
HG-20:NC: Check the wiring: does the E-stop NC contact go to the board input PA10? (y/n)
HG-20:NO: Check the wiring: does the E-stop NO contact go +5V_CUT -> 68 Ω resistor -> diode D2 -> driver ENA+? (y/n)
HG-20:D1: Check the wiring: is diode D1 in the board's ENA wire and a 10 kΩ resistor from ENA+ to logic GND? (y/n)
HG-20:NOK1: Is there NO contactor in the 48 V line, and can the observer reach the 48 V mains switch? (y/n)
HG-20:NOMCU: Does the E-stop NO path to ENA+ run without any part controlled by the Nucleo? (y/n)
HG-20:LABEL: Is the panel labelled, the E-stop a red mushroom on yellow, and PAUSE a separate button? (y/n)
*:M-5iso: Multimeter on the highest ohm range. Measure between 48 V GND (PSU 0 V) and the Nucleo GND (picture B2). Type the value in MΩ (OL = type 999).
*:M5-PSU-ON: Observer: switch the 48 V ON. The motor holds; nothing moves. Keep a hand near the red E-stop.
*:M-5: Multimeter on volts DC. Measure the +5V_CUT output of the small DC-DC converter against logic GND (picture B2). Type the value (about 5.0 V).
*:M5-PSU-OFF: Observer: switch the 48 V OFF again.
HG-31:INIT: Answer y only if Implementer A's statement says: in every image the header pins are digital inputs without pull-up (never analog).
P2-ENTRY:P2: Phase 2 starts: observer switches the 48 V ON. No specimen, nothing in the travel; the observer stays at the red E-stop.
*:PSU-OFF: Observer: switch the 48 V power supply OFF at its mains switch, then press Enter.
*:PSU-ON: Observer: switch the 48 V power supply ON at its mains switch, wait 2 s, then press Enter.
*:PUL-SHUNT: The 48 V is OFF. At the driver terminal, lift the PUL- wire from logic GND and put the 100 Ω shunt between PUL- and logic GND (picture B4). Take a photo.
*:DIR-SHUNT: The 48 V is OFF. At the driver terminal, lift the DIR- wire from logic GND and put the 100 Ω shunt between DIR- and logic GND (picture B4). Take a photo.
*:ENA-SHUNT: The 48 V is OFF. At the driver terminal, lift the ENA- wire from logic GND and put the 100 Ω shunt between ENA- and logic GND (picture B4). Take a photo.
*:PUL-VOH: Multimeter on volts DC: red probe on the driver terminal PUL+, black on logic GND (picture B4). Type the value.
*:DIR-VOH: Multimeter on volts DC: red probe on the driver terminal DIR+, black on logic GND (picture B4). Type the value.
*:ENA-VOH: Multimeter on volts DC: red probe on the driver terminal ENA+, black on logic GND (picture B4). Type the value.
*:PUL-ILED: Multimeter on volts DC: measure across the 100 Ω shunt (red probe at PUL-, black at GND, picture B4). Type the value in mV.
*:DIR-ILED: Multimeter on volts DC: measure across the 100 Ω shunt (red probe at DIR-, black at GND, picture B4). Type the value in mV.
*:ENA-ILED: Multimeter on volts DC: measure across the 100 Ω shunt (red probe at ENA-, black at GND, picture B4). Type the value in mV.
*:PUL-RESTORE: The 48 V is still OFF. Remove the shunt and connect PUL- to logic GND again (picture B4). Take a photo.
*:DIR-RESTORE: The 48 V is still OFF. Remove the shunt and connect DIR- to logic GND again (picture B4). Take a photo.
*:ENA-RESTORE: The 48 V is still OFF. Remove the shunt and connect ENA- to logic GND again (picture B4). Take a photo.
*:JUMPERS: Change the jumper wires on the measurement header MH exactly as written below (picture B1, step table). Nothing else.
*:TAPS: Move the four header taps J-PUL-A, J-PUL-B, J-DIR and J-ENA to the outputs of the buffer board (picture B1).
HG-07:FREE: Operator: turn the motor coupling gently by hand. Does it turn freely (no holding force)? (y/n)
HG-07:HOLD: Operator: turn the motor coupling gently by hand. Does it hold now? (y/n)
HG-10cd:c1: Observer: press and HOLD the black RESET button B2 on the Nucleo, then press the red E-stop with the other hand. Operator: turn the coupling gently by hand. Is it FREE? (y/n) (picture B6)
HG-10cd:M-1: Keep RESET held and the E-stop pressed. Multimeter on volts DC across the 68 Ω resistor R_E (picture B2, M-1). Type the value (about 0.7 V).
HG-10cd:M-3b: Keep both held. Multimeter on volts DC at the Nucleo pin PA4 (CN8-3) against GND (picture B2, M-3). Type the value.
HG-10cd:M-4p: Keep both held. Multimeter on volts DC at the driver terminal ENA+ against GND (picture B2, M-4). Type the value (4.0-4.6 V).
HG-10cd:c2: Operator: HANDS OFF the shaft. Observer: keep RESET held and release the E-stop. Does the shaft hold again? (y/n)
HG-10cd:c3: Observer: release the RESET button. Wait 2 s; the runner reconnects.
HG-10cd:M-2a: The board runs and the driver is enabled. Multimeter: the ENA loop current through the 100 Ω shunt in ENA- (picture B2, M-2). Type the value in mA (about 0).
HG-10cd:c3-press: Observer: press the red E-stop (the board is running).
HG-10cd:M-2c: E-stop pressed. Multimeter: the ENA loop current again (picture B2, M-2). Type the value in mA.
HG-10cd:M-3c: E-stop pressed. Multimeter on volts DC at the Nucleo pin PA4 (picture B2, M-3). Type the value.
HG-10cd:c3-free: Observer: release the E-stop. Operator: turn the coupling by hand. Is it still FREE (the board keeps the driver off until cleared)? (y/n)
HG-10cd:c3-hold: Hands off. After the runner cleared the E-stop and enabled the driver: does the shaft hold? (y/n)
*:PRESS-HOLD: Observer: press the red E-stop and keep it pressed for at least 2 s.
*:ESTOP-RELEASE: If the red E-stop is pressed: turn it to release it.
HG-10b:PRESS: Observer: when you see NOW, press the red E-stop at once (the table is moving).
HG-10b:e0: Observer: press the red E-stop SLOWLY - about 1 s half-way, then fully - and hold it.
HG-10b:e1: Observer: press the red E-stop QUICKLY past the first point, then fully, and hold it.
HG-18:PRESS: Observer: when you see NOW, press the red E-stop at once (the table is moving).
HG-30:PRESS: Observer: when you see NOW, press the red E-stop at once (the table is moving).
HG-30:FREE: Operator: turn the coupling gently by hand. Is it free? (y/n)
HG-30:SPRING: Is the spring specimen fitted for the load-limit repeat? (y/n)
HG-30:HG31: Do the header jumpers stay fitted while the release image runs, as Implementer A states (no pin in analog mode)? (y/n)
HG-18:PRESS-IDLE: Observer: when you see NOW, press the red E-stop (the table is standing, the driver is on).
*:PAUSE: Observer: when you see NOW, press the PAUSE button (the table is moving).
BENCH-ENTRY:P-1: Before the stimulus trials (picture B3, P-1): no specimen, no load, no tool in the travel; operator at the PC, observer at the red E-stop and the 48 V switch; both limit switches plugged in. Type both names.
*:P-3: Observer: switch the 48 V OFF. Unplug the E-stop sense plug at the interface board, plug the J-STIM wire into that socket, hang the tag 'E-STOP SENSE BYPASSED - TEST' on the red button, take a photo (picture B3, P-3).
*:P-4R: Type the value of the resistor in the J-STIM wire (picture B3, P-4; should be 220 Ω).
*:P-4V: Multimeter on volts DC at the Nucleo pin PA10 (CN10-33) against GND (picture B3, P-4). Type the value.
*:P-6: Observer: switch the 48 V ON and keep one hand on the red E-stop (it still cuts the driver) and one near the 48 V switch (picture B3, P-6).
*:RC-ESTOP: Change the header jumpers as written below (pictures B1 / B3); J-STIM stays in the E-stop socket.
*:RC-ESTOP-2: Change the header jumpers as written below (picture B1).
*:P-8a: Observer: switch the 48 V OFF. Remove the J-STIM wire, plug the E-stop sense plug back in, remove the tag, take a photo (picture B3, P-8).
*:P-8c: Observer: press the red E-stop (the board is running).
*:RC-LIMIT_START: Unplug the START switch, plug the J-STIM wire into its socket, and change the header jumpers as written below (pictures B3 / B1).
*:RC-LIMIT_END: Unplug the END switch, plug the J-STIM wire into its socket, and change the header jumpers as written below (pictures B3 / B1).
*:RC-PAUSE: Unplug the PAUSE button, plug the J-STIM wire into its socket, and change the header jumpers as written below (pictures B3 / B1).
*:RC-LIMIT_START-RESTORE: Remove the J-STIM wire and plug the START switch back in.
*:RC-LIMIT_END-RESTORE: Remove the J-STIM wire and plug the END switch back in.
*:RC-PAUSE-RESTORE: Remove the J-STIM wire and plug the PAUSE button back in.
*:START-STIM: Unplug the START switch and plug the J-STIM wire into its socket; header jumpers as written below (pictures B3 / B1). The red E-stop keeps working normally.
*:END-STIM: Unplug the END switch and plug the J-STIM wire into its socket; header jumpers as written below (pictures B3 / B1). The red E-stop keeps working normally.
*:START-REAL: Remove the J-STIM wire and plug the START switch back in (J-EVT stays where it is, picture B1).
*:END-REAL: Remove the J-STIM wire and plug the END switch back in (J-EVT stays where it is, picture B1).
HG-17:BREAK-estop: Operator: when you see NOW, pull the E-stop sense plug out at the interface board (the table jogs slowly).
HG-17:BREAK-start: Operator: when you see NOW, pull the START switch plug out (the table jogs slowly).
HG-17:BREAK-end: Operator: when you see NOW, pull the END switch plug out (the table jogs slowly).
HG-17:FIX-estop: Plug the E-stop sense plug back in.
HG-17:FIX-start: Plug the START switch plug back in.
HG-17:FIX-end: Plug the END switch plug back in.
HG-17:NO-LIFT: Observer: switch the 48 V OFF. At the E-stop, lift the NO wire (the one going to R_E) from its terminal and insulate the free end (picture B6).
HG-17:NO-PSU-ON: Observer: switch the 48 V ON, then hold the Nucleo RESET button B2 and press the red E-stop.
HG-17:NO-BREAK: Operator: turn the coupling by hand. Does the shaft still HOLD? (y = holds; this is expected: a broken NO wire is not noticed by anything)
HG-17:NO-FIX: Operator: hands off. Observer: release the E-stop and RESET, switch the 48 V OFF, put the NO wire back on its terminal, switch the 48 V ON (picture B6).
HG-17:NO-C1: Check again: observer holds RESET and presses the E-stop, operator turns the coupling. Is it FREE now? (y/n)
HG-17:NO-DONE: Operator: hands off. Observer: release the E-stop, then RESET (the board restarts).
HG-04:READY: Observer: hand on the red E-stop. After you press Enter the runner prints GO and saves to the board memory for about half a second: press the E-stop as soon as you see GO.
HG-04:PRESS: GO - press the red E-stop NOW.
HG-16:ALM-V-off: Multimeter on volts DC at the Nucleo pin PA8 (ALM input) against GND, driver unpowered (picture B2). Type the value.
HG-16:PEND-V-off: Multimeter on volts DC at the Nucleo pin PA9 (PEND input) against GND, driver unpowered (picture B2). Type the value.
HG-16:ALM-V-on: Multimeter on volts DC at PA8, driver powered and standing. Type the value.
HG-16:PEND-V-on: Multimeter on volts DC at PA9, driver powered, in position. Type the value.
HG-16:LEVELS: Type what the runner should keep for the ALM / PEND polarity ('keep' unless the readings say otherwise).
HG-24:PROVOKE: Make the driver show an alarm on purpose (e.g. with the 48 V OFF unplug the motor phase plug, then 48 V ON) and type how you did it.
HG-24:PWRCYCLE: Reset the driver alarm: observer switches the 48 V OFF, waits 5 s, switches it ON again.
HG-24:PWRRES: Is the driver's alarm LED off now? (y/n)
HG-24:ENATOG: Make the alarm again; the runner switches the driver off and on. Type the result: 'cleared' or 'not cleared'.
HG-21:FITTED: Is the optional 48 V presence sense on PA7 fitted? (normally n)
HG-23:INSP: Is the SN74ACT244 buffer board installed? (normally n - it is fitted only if the bring-up qualification failed)
HG-28:PREP: No specimen, nothing in the travel; caliper ready (picture B9); observer hand at the red E-stop.
HG-28:DIR: Did the table move AWAY from the START switch? (y/n)
HG-28:CAL: Caliper: measure between the two marked faces after the move and subtract the reading before (picture B9). Type D1 - D0 in mm.
HG-28:INV-OK: Next, the runner homes with the direction setting deliberately WRONG: the table runs AWAY from START toward the END switch, slowly. Observer: hand on the red E-stop. Go ahead? (y/n)
HG-28:SAVE: The direction setting was changed: save it permanently in the board now? (y)
HG-09:CAL0: Caliper between the marked faces (picture B9): type D1 - D0 of the last move in mm.
HG-09:CAL1: Caliper between the marked faces (picture B9): type D1 - D0 of the last move in mm.
HG-09:CAL2: Caliper between the marked faces (picture B9): type D1 - D0 of the last move in mm.
HG-09:CAL3: Caliper between the marked faces (picture B9): type D1 - D0 of the last move in mm.
HG-09:CAL5: Caliper between the marked faces (picture B9): type D1 - D0 of the last move in mm.
HG-09:CAL6: Caliper between the marked faces (picture B9): type D1 - D0 of the last move in mm.
HG-09:CAL7: Caliper between the marked faces (picture B9): type D1 - D0 of the last move in mm.
HG-09:CAL8: Caliper between the marked faces (picture B9): type D1 - D0 of the last move in mm.
HG-09:CAL9: Caliper between the marked faces (picture B9): type D1 - D0 of the last move in mm.
HG-09:CAL4: Caliper between the marked faces (picture B9): type D1 - D0 of the last move in mm.
*:SPRING: With the driver disabled (as the runner says): fit the spring between the load cell and the table so that a move away from START pulls it (picture B8). Never stand in line with the spring when it is loaded. Observer: hand on the red E-stop.
HG-15:DIAL: Set the dial indicator on its magnetic stand on the frame, plunger on the +x face of the table, about 1 mm pre-travel, and zero it (picture B8).
HG-15:NRST: Observer: press the black RESET button B2 on the Nucleo once (about 1 s) and release it (picture B7). Hands off the table and the spring.
HG-15:PWR: Unplug the USB cable at the Nucleo for at least 5 s, then plug it back in (picture B7). The 48 V stays ON. Hands off the table and the spring.
HG-15:DIAL-PIN: Read the dial indicator now (picture B8). Type the value in mm.
HG-15:DIAL-POWER: Read the dial indicator now (picture B8). Type the value in mm.
HG-15:DIAL-IWDG: Read the dial indicator now (picture B8). Type the value in mm.
HG-25:CAL: Has the travel calibration been done with the PC software wizard (bring-up guide section 11.1)? (y/n)
HG-25:NOSPEC: With the driver disabled: remove the spring specimen (picture B8). Nothing in the travel afterwards.
HG-25:DIAL0: Set the dial indicator against the table at 10 mm and zero it (picture B8).
HG-25:DIAL1: Read the dial indicator after the very slow move (picture B8). Type the value in mm.
HG-25:CAL0: Caliper between the marked faces at 20 mm: note D0 (picture B9).
HG-25:CAL50: Caliper between the marked faces after the 50 mm move: type D1 - D0 in mm (picture B9).
HG-25:TRAVEL: Measure the whole travel of the last move (soft-min to soft-max) with the caliper or a scale (picture B9). Type it in mm.
HG-26:DIAL: Set the dial indicator against the table at the home position (x = 0) and zero it (picture B8).
HG-26:DIAL0: Read the dial indicator at the home position. Type the value in mm.
HG-26:DIAL1: Read the dial indicator at the home position. Type the value in mm.
HG-26:DIAL2: Read the dial indicator at the home position. Type the value in mm.
HG-26:DIAL3: Read the dial indicator at the home position. Type the value in mm.
HG-26:DIAL4: Read the dial indicator at the home position. Type the value in mm.
HG-26:DIAL5: Read the dial indicator at the home position. Type the value in mm.
HG-26:DIAL6: Read the dial indicator at the home position. Type the value in mm.
HG-26:DIAL7: Read the dial indicator at the home position. Type the value in mm.
HG-26:DIAL8: Read the dial indicator at the home position. Type the value in mm.
HG-26:DIAL9: Read the dial indicator at the home position. Type the value in mm.
*:HOME-CONFIRM: The board refused to home because the load cell shows an offset. Is the axis really unloaded (no specimen, nothing touching)? y = home anyway.
